newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest power prices ease in quiet talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest power prices ease in quiet talk.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Midwest mostly eased Wednesday in quiet trade as warmer weather moved through parts of the region, industry sources said.
Temperatures were reported to have returned to near-normal levels Wednesday and were expected to remain that way through the Thanksgiving Day holiday, but fall to below-normal levels from Dec 1 to 5.
Trade was reported to be relatively thin ahead of the Thanksgiving Day holiday on Thursday and with many traders planning to take Friday off.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm next day power deals for Friday delivery were notionally pegged steady at $25.00-27.00, the brokers and marketers said.
Round-the-clock power through to the end of the weekend was talked at $14.00-16.00, the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power deals were notionally pegged steady in the $12.00-14.00 range, the sources said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) peak, non-firm power for Friday delivery was pegged at $23.00-25.00 from next-day delivery talk on Tuesday of $27.00-31.00 per MWh.
Round-the clock power through to the end of the weekend was assessed at $14.50-16.50, the sources said.
MAIN off peak power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Friday and Monday delivery was assessed at $22.00-23.00 from next day delivery talk on Tuesday of $25.00-27.00, the sources said.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00.
December peak ECAR was talked steady at $22.00-23.00, with January/February ECAR was also assessed steady at $23.00-24.00 per MWh.
Peak non-firm power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) for Friday delivery were talked steady at $27.00-29.00, the sources said, while Monday peak power was pegged at $26.00-27.50.
December SPP was assessed steady at $24.00-26.50, while January/February was pegged unchanged at $27.00-27.50 per MWh.
